text_blocks.speaker: Chris Mannix
text_blocks.text: Do you look at them as a top-tier contender, up there with San Antonio and maybe Houston in the Western Conference, or are you seeing some things that might make you want to bump them down a notch?

text_blocks.speaker: Evan Turner
text_blocks.text: For one, to be compared to San Antonio, you have to be literally elite, or you're going to have that one X-factor that can send you over the top, which they do with Luka Dončić. It comes down to, can he do it? Is his availability going to be there when it comes down to May? I think one thing I've noticed about that team, it's been fun, but I think the same thing that makes you laugh, makes you cry. Sometimes they have home run moments. You have the Quentin Grimes that will drop 47 points to beat a struggling Charlotte Hornets team. You'll have the superstar Luka Dončić averaging the best stat lines in 50-something years. You'll have Austin Reaves when he comes back being healthy, but I think sometimes when it comes down to it, it's like, you have to stop relying on the special stuff and you have to rely on what your identity is going to be.

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on Walker Kessler's defensive importance to the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: If he goes out, he's just as irreplaceable to me as Luka Dončić.
quotes.quote: Where I get concerned though is what I see the lapses I sometimes see on the defensive end. They are a very opportunistic defense. They are among the top five teams in steals, blocks, and I think number one in steals. They play the passing games extremely well. But defensive rating, they're in the bottom third of the NBA. They turn the ball over a lot, bottom 10 in the league in turnovers, and the bench doesn't produce all that much. Now some of that of course is Austin Reaves when he comes back, it will bump some production down to that bench. But they've got some warning signs there. Walker Kessler has been pretty healthy for most of the season, but he's been injured in the past, most recently most of last season. And if he goes out, he's just as irreplaceable to me as Luka Dončić. That sounds blasphemous, but who do they have that can step into that Walker Kessler role and give them rebounding, shot-blocking, clean up things on the defensive end?

quotes.speaker: Chris Mannix
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Mannix on the Lakers' need for Walker Kessler's defensive presence
quotes.excerpt: You got him to be a defensive anchor to clean up a lot of the mistakes
quotes.quote: He's going to get Victor Wembanyama a couple of times. He's going to get Alperen Şengün a couple of times. He's going to get Nikola Jokić a couple of times. He's going to get Rudy Gobert a couple of times. This is why they got him, not to beat up on the Sacramento Kings or to play against the Jazz or to fight off the Clippers. You got him to be a defensive anchor to clean up a lot of the mistakes that your guards make, but also to match up with these high-level centers. And there are some high-level centers coming down the pipe over the next month of the Lakers. That's what's going to be key for Walker Kessler.
